title: When the Contact Falls
premise: Sable Marchetti, a freelance interpreter who handles the delegations governments prefer to disown, is summoned to a summit in Trieste that everyone privately expects to collapse. When his old handler, Ivo Kessler, is found dead in the harbor — yet sends Sable a calendar invitation for a meeting the next morning — Sable realizes the death was staged and the 'accident' planned for the summit's final day is anything but. Torn between the delegation he's sworn to serve and the truth Kessler died protecting, Sable uncovers a plot inside his own service to detonate a ferry and blame the peace faction. In the end, Sable betrays his employers to save both sides, exposes the conspirators with Kessler's dead-man's-switch archive, and walks away from the intelligence world entirely — choosing belonging over duty at last.
about_author: Lena Okonkwo is a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths in cities where ceasefires were signed and quietly broken. She writes thrillers about the people paid to translate other people's lies.

chapters.title: The Booth
chapters.summary: Sable Marchetti interprets a hostile pre-summit briefing in Geneva, smoothing over an insult that could derail everything. POV: Sable. Establishes his gift for making enemies sound almost honest, and his exhaustion with work no one will claim. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Cases No One Wants
chapters.summary: Sable meets his handler, Ivo Kessler, in a rain-soaked parking garage; Ivo hints the Trieste delegation is 'already dead' and slips him a burner phone without explanation. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: unease — Ivo has never been careless before.

chapters.title: Trieste
chapters.summary: The delegation arrives in Trieste; Sable reads the room during the welcome reception and notices security details that don't match the official roster. POV: Sable, with a brief interlude from deputy head of delegation Amara Diallo. Emotional beat: the shimmer of hope the summit might actually matter.

chapters.title: Dead Water
chapters.summary: Ivo Kessler is pulled from the harbor, officially a drowning. Sable identifies the body and is told to go home. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion when he spots bruising on Ivo's wrists that the report ignores.

chapters.title: Tomorrow, 09:00
chapters.summary: That night, Sable's phone buzzes: a calendar invitation from Ivo's account for a meeting tomorrow morning — sent after the death. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: cold fear; either Ivo is alive or someone wants Sable in a specific place at a specific time.

chapters.title: The Empty Room
chapters.summary: Sable keeps the meeting: an abandoned customs office where he finds Ivo's hidden notes and a partial ferry manifest — the Adriana Star, chartered for the summit's closing excursion. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: vertigo as the 'accident' takes shape.

chapters.title: Amara
chapters.summary: Sable tests Amara Diallo with a translated half-truth; she reveals she suspects her own security chief, Brandt, of reporting to someone outside the delegation. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: reluctant trust between two people trained to distrust.

chapters.title: Brandt's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable breaks into Brandt's quarters and photographs a ledger of payments routed through a shell company tied to his own intelligence service. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: betrayal — the threat wears his own colors.

chapters.title: Debriefed
chapters.summary: Sable is summoned by service liaison Colonel Voss, who warns him off 'conspiracy theories' and offers him a ticket home. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the trap tightening; refusing means becoming a suspect.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing Ivo's notes, Sable confirms the Adriana Star's manifest was altered to overload the closing-day excursion with both delegations' principals. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: horror at how clean the design is — one explosion, two peace processes ended.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Dead
chapters.summary: The burner rings: Ivo, alive, hoarse, hiding. He explains he faked his death when the plot reached him and that the archive proving it sits behind a dead-man's switch only Sable can now arm. POV: Ivo (phone call). Emotional beat: relief braided with fury at being used as a pawn again.

chapters.title: Loyalty Audit
chapters.summary: Voss has Sable followed; his hotel room is searched and the ledger photos nearly discovered. He hides them inside his interpreting notes. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: paranoia — every colleague is now a possible watcher.

chapters.title: What Amara Knows
chapters.summary: Amara confronts Sable with what she's found about Brandt; they form an uneasy alliance, each withholding one crucial fact. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared danger, and guilt over the secrets between them.

chapters.title: The Mole's Price
chapters.summary: Brandt catches Sable copying files; a tense standoff ends when Sable bluffs that copies are already outside the country. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: terror mastered by performance — his interpreter's skills turned lethal.

chapters.title: Voss's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Sable realizes Voss isn't corrupt but calculating: the attack serves a faction that prefers a frozen conflict to a fragile peace. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: chilling conviction — the antagonist believes he is saving lives.

chapters.title: Arming the Switch
chapters.summary: Meeting Ivo in a boatyard, Sable arms the dead-man's-switch archive set to release to three newspapers if Ivo dies for real. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into commitment — no more unattributed cases.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Ivo is captured; Brandt's team sweeps the city, and Amara covers Sable's escape at real cost to her standing. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: love against duty crystallizing — she chooses Sable over protocol.

chapters.title: Closing Day
chapters.summary: The final session convenes; the Adriana Star waits at the pier, and Sable must warn both principals without triggering the plotters to accelerate. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: clock-ticking dread as speeches drone on.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: Sable engineers a translation 'error' that forces an unscheduled delay, buying time while Amara pulls the principals off the excursion list. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: audacity — using his booth as a weapon.

chapters.title: When the Contact Falls
chapters.summary: Climax aboard the docked ferry: Brandt moves the timetable up; Sable confronts him below decks, and Ivo — escaping custody — arrives to trigger the archive live. Brandt is arrested; the bomb's trigger man flees into the crowd. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: violent clarity, everything staked at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The archive publishes; Voss resigns rather than face inquiry, and the summit limps to a modest but real agreement. Sable testifies anonymously, his name kept out of it one last time. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: hollow victory, grief for Ivo's ruined life.

chapters.title: Boothless
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Sable declines reassignment and instead teaches interpretation in Trieste; Amara visits, and they begin something unhurried and honest. He finally belongs somewhere no one needs him to translate. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
